subject: Post-call — model & prompt samples / next steps for Atlas Search
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Priya Chandra <priya@atlassearch.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Nov 2025 16:23:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap + ask: prompts & redaction guidance

Hi Priya — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have alignment:

Key takeaways
- Primary use: improving semantic search relevance and generating short executive summaries for internal content (support articles + legal snippets).
- Volume profile: ~15M searches/month; typical query length 5–20 tokens, bursty peak traffic during launches.
- Main success metrics: relevance NDCG@10 and summary accuracy (precision of extracted named entities).
- Main concerns: redaction of PII in summaries, preventing quality regressions during model swaps, and cost predictability.

Proposed immediate deliverables (we can start within a week):
1) Redwood: shortlist of 3 recommended model variants tuned for semantic search + summarization, with benchmark links and cost/latency estimates.
2) Atlas: sample prompt set (representative queries + edge cases) and ~20 redaction-sensitive examples so we can validate PII handling.
3) Joint: 2-week pilot plan (see attached) that runs evals on your sample prompts and our benchmarks, plus suggested guardrails for redaction.

Can you share: the three prompt buckets you mentioned on the call ("short search queries", "long conversational queries", "doc-summarize-with-redaction") and any example prompts you already have? If possible, include a few examples with sensitive fields (we'll treat these strictly for eval and can sign an NDA if needed).

Attachment: initial-eval-plan.pdf (high level timeline + success criteria)

Next step: If that works, I’ll loop in Marissa to put together model recommendations and cost/benchmark links. Suggest a follow-up slot next Wednesday — 30 minutes to confirm the sample prompts and the pilot scope.

Thanks again,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

---
This message and attachments are intended only for the recipient and contain product evaluation material.

From: Priya Chandra <priya@atlassearch.com>

Date: Wed, 13 Nov 2025 09:07:00 -0800

Thanks Hannah — great summary and appreciate the clear next steps. Quick notes and I've attached an initial export of example queries: search-prompts.csv.

What I attached
- search-prompts.csv: 120 rows across the three buckets we discussed (short/long/summarize). There are 20 flagged as "PII" — these are anonymized but keep them only for evaluation.
- A short internal note on our redaction needs (sensitive_fields.txt) — not attached here, but I can share if you need more context.

Questions before we proceed
1) For the redaction check: do you prefer we send examples with placeholders (e.g., <EMAIL>, <SSN>) or real-looking but anonymized values? We can do either.
2) On regressions: how will we surface potential regressions if we change model families during the pilot? What metrics will you run by default?

We'd prefer the placeholder approach for any items that can't leave our environment. If you can confirm how Redwood will log/evaluate PII examples and whether those are retained, that would help us finalize the sample set.

I’m happy to give you access to a shared Drive folder (I’ll add Marissa’s redwood email when you confirm).

Thanks,
Priya Chandra
Head of Search Engineering | Atlas Search
priya@atlassearch.com | +1 617-555-2290

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + ask: prompts & redaction guidance

Hannah / team — taking this on. Quick model recommendations based on Atlas profile:

Recommended shortlist
- rwd-text-compact-1.1 (quantized): best cost/latency for high-throughput semantic search; strong ANN embedding alignment in our benchmarks.
- rwd-text-balance-2 (FP16): better for mixed search + short summaries where entity fidelity matters.
- rwd-summarize-lex-2 (FP16, tuned): specialized for extractive summarization with guardrails for redaction.

Benchmarks & links
- Latency/cost: https://benchmarks.redwood.ai/semantic-search/atlas-sample
- Embedding quality evals (pairwise NDCG): https://drive.google.com/file/d/drive-benchmarks-id
- Model protection & rollback playbook: https://docs.redwood.com/rollback-playbook

Attachments: model-benchmarks.md (contains warmup profiles, expected TP50/99 and estimated token cost for pilot).

On regressions: I recommend we run the following by default in the pilot:
- NDCG@10 on your short/long query buckets (baseline run on your CSV).
- Entity recall/precision on the 20 PII-flagged rows.
- Human spot check: sample 30 summaries for hallucination and redaction failures (we can do a shared spreadsheet).

Infra recommendation (Dylan)
- Start pilot on Redwood Dedicated; if Atlas prefers no shared infra we can deploy the eval into a Private VPC for the two weeks — that only needs a short procurement note.

I’ll upload the detailed benchmarks and cost model to the Drive folder Hannah mentioned and paste the link in the HubSpot deal.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Principal Applied ML | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
